1.note: The line ends again with נַפְשִׁי ("my soul"), as the line before. Read here from the verb נָפַשׁ, "to rest, be refreshed" (Exod 31:17), for the rhyme with חָפְשִׁי. "In the days of my delight and of my soul" is also possible.

2.note: Uncertain. Read שָׁנֶיהָ as "its scarlet" (שָׁנִי, as in Prov 31:21 לְבֻשָׁה שָׁנִים), the red flowers set in the green. The pointing also allows "its years".

3.note: A play on אֹהָלִים "tents" and אֲהָלוֹת "aloes" (Song 4:14; Num 24:5-6 has both words close together): arbors made of aloes wood.

4.note: Literally "they have, of their pearls, a bell": the seeds are the pearls, and the bell-shaped rind holds them. Bells and pomegranates alternate on the hem of the high priest's robe (Exod 28:33-34), as in the poem below.

5.note: Isa 15:9: "the waters of Dimon are full of blood". The juice is red as blood.

6.note: Pointed מִפָּנֵינוּ, "before us". Unpointed, the same letters can be read מִפְּנִינוּ, "of our pearls", a play on the pearls (seeds) two lines before.

7.note: Literally "and then he finds vengeances": the one who cracks the stubborn nut is paid back for its hardness. The subject may also be the nut ("it meets its punishment").

8.note: From Song 7:8 זֹאת קוֹמָתֵךְ דָּמְתָה לְתָמָר. Kaminka's edition prints lines 115-116 as one verse line, "וכפגעי יעלת חן אומר / זאת קומתך דמתה תמר", which continues the rhyme in -מר of the poem. Our text has two prose lines, without זאת; it is kept as it is.

9.note: Uncertain. The line rhymes אֶשְׁכּוֹל with itself. מְכוֹן עוֹלָם recalls the Temple (1 Kgs 8:13 מְכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים), at whose entrance a golden vine with clusters was hung (m. Middot 3:8). The exact sense is not clear.

10.note: Job 41:17, of Leviathan, an obscure phrase ("by reason of breakings they purify themselves" or "they cringe at the crashing"). Here the kernels come out of the broken shell clean.

11.note: Her cheek is dawn (שְׁחָרִים) and her hair is evening (עֲרָבִים, "evenings"; compare the poem below, "her hair is night"). שחרים also suggests "black", and עֲרָבִים recalls עָרֵב, "sweet".
